mechanism: `testProperties(id)` attaches a stable `accessibilityLabel` (Android) / `testID` (iOS) to elements; applied consistently across every screen read for this audit (Home, DataManagement, LoginForm, FormComponents, PermissionSwitches, TabSideMenu).
expected_behavior: Every interactive element carries a stable, platform-appropriate automation identifier discoverable by an accessibility-id-based mobile driver.
notes: Automation-affordance evidence; cited under Cross-cutting Properties section 4 (Automation Affordances, Observability).

mechanism: The Data Management screen exposes four independently addressable state tiers (in-memory, AsyncStorage-tier SQLite, explicit SQLite, SecureStore/Keychain-Keystore), each with a testID-tagged input, a testID-tagged 'Save' control (`data-<tier>-save`) that establishes a known value, and a testID-tagged 'Clear' control (`data-<tier>-clear`; the SecureStore one literally labelled 'Clear (test hook)') that resets the tier to a known empty state.
expected_behavior: After Save, testID `data-<tier>-readout` shows exactly the saved text. After Clear, the same readout shows the fixed placeholder text (`— empty —` for memory; `— nothing saved yet —` for the three persisted tiers). Persistence-on-restart and persistence-on-reinstall differ per tier exactly as the in-screen help text documents (memory: cleared on process kill; AsyncStorage/SQLite tiers: cleared by app-data clear or `mobile: clearApp`, not by navigation; SecureStore: survives restart, cleared by uninstall on Android).
notes: Primary Score 3 evidence for this modality (protocol/capability-rubric-v1.md, Decision procedure step 3: establish/reset + defined expected outcome). No EXECUTION_VERIFIED record was produced; SOURCE_VERIFIED is fully obtainable for this open-source component and is the confirming status used (confirmation_state = CONFIRMED). No app-wide 'reset all tiers' action was found; only the four per-tier Clear controls (see Resetability, section 4). Considered and rejected: reading this as merely 'the end-user path' (cross-cutting-properties-v1.md's State Controllability definition) rather than an SUT-exposed experimental mechanism — rejected because the screen's own text names Appium/`mobile: clearApp` expectations directly and labels the SecureStore action 'Clear (test hook)', i.e. the SUT documents this control as a test hook, not an incidental UI flow; flagged for adjudication regardless (unresolved.md, SUT-06-U05).

mechanism: Camera/Microphone/Location/Photo-library switches (testIDs `permission-switch-<name>`) call the corresponding Expo `requestXPermissionsAsync()`; the OS permission dialog is a real, documented Android/iOS system dialog, not a mock.
expected_behavior: On grant, the switch reflects `result.granted === true`, observable via the same testID. Revoking is not exposed in-app: toggling off when already granted calls `Linking.openSettings()` and reverts the switch (README.md confirms: 'Revoking access afterward is only possible in the device settings').
notes: Establish/activate side of the mechanism is SUT-exposed and verifiable; reset (revoke) is not, so this record alone supports Score 2, not Score 3 (Score 3 is reached for this modality via SUT06-EV-0007 instead).

mechanism: MainActivity's intent-filter registers `android:scheme="wdio"` (also `exp+wdiodemoapp`); app.json sets `expo.scheme: "wdio"`; Expo Router's file-based routes under `app/(tabs)/` (index, webview, login, forms, swipe, drag, permissions, data-management) each correspond to a routable screen name.
expected_behavior: A `wdio://<route>` URL (for example `wdio://data-management`) opens the app directly on that screen, per Expo Router's documented file-based deep-linking behavior.
notes: Scheme registration and route files are source-confirmed at the pinned commit; actual deep-link routing behavior was not executed/observed in this audit (Expo Router's link-resolution behavior is itself a dependency, not this repository's own code). Not used to raise this cell beyond Score 2 on its own. src/App.tsx also defines a `linking` config for `wdio://`, but that file is dead code: it is imported by neither index.js (`expo-router/entry`) nor any file under app/, so it is not part of the evaluated app's actual behavior. See unresolved.md SUT-06-U02.

mechanism: The Menu side-panel lists every screen with a star toggle per entry (testID `side-menu-star-<name>`) that pins/unpins the screen in the bottom tab bar via `TabBarMenuContext`'s `togglePinned`; each menu row and each star is independently testID-addressable (`side-menu-item-<name>`).
expected_behavior: Toggling a star deterministically adds/removes that screen from the bottom tab bar (observable via the tab bar's own testIDs) without restarting the app.
notes: Automation-affordance / in-app configuration-state evidence.

mechanism: Login/Sign-up validation is deterministic and local: email must match a fixed regex, password length must be >= 8, and (sign-up only) the confirmation field must equal the password.
expected_behavior: Invalid input produces a field-level shake animation and a rule-specific `errorMessage` (testIDs `input-email`, `input-password`, `input-repeat-password`); valid input produces a fixed 1500ms simulated delay then a deterministic `Alert` ('You are logged in!' or 'You successfully signed up!').
notes: No backend call is involved (see SUT06-EV-0004); the 1500ms delay is time-dependent for UI timing only, the pass/fail outcome itself is deterministic. Cited under Determinism, section 4.

mechanism: The WebView tab loads a fixed external URL (`https://webdriver.io/`) with `webviewDebuggingEnabled` and `originWhitelist: ['*']`; README.md documents this screen as built specifically 'to test for example switching context and interacting with the WebView' (opened once).
expected_behavior: A stable, documented context-switch scenario: the native WebView container is reachable by a mobile driver and its content (the webdriver.io site) is reachable by a web-context driver after switching context.
notes: The scenario's own content (the external site) is an external dependency outside the SUT's control (cited under Determinism, external dependency); the presence of the scenario itself is what this record supports.
